To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The POD-Galerkin method is an effective tool for deriving hierarchies of ordinary differential equations from the spherical quasi-geo-strophic equations, and 2) the most effective POD-Galerkin truncation for approximating the data is the one that uses a vertical truncation of the spherical quasi geostrophic model that includes the barotropic mode, the leading order baro-clinic mode, and a second order baroclinically stable mode.

(1) the POD-Galerkin model is capable of reproducing the observed baroclinic instability of the Mars atmosphere, and that (2) this instability is a Hopf bifurcation, which is consistent with the diagnostic analysis.
the model is chaotic for all truncations, that the model is more chaotic for larger vertical truncations and that the Galerkin truncation has a negligible impact on the chaotic nature of the model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the derivation of reduced-order models of the baroclically unstable atmosphere, which can be solved numerically and which capture the essential features of the original system.
the development of a simplified, yet physically relevant, mathematical model of the Martian climate, and its subsequent analysis.
the derivation, analysis, and numerical simulation of a hierarchy of nonlinear ordinary differential equation approximations to the dynamics of the Mars atmospheric circulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system based on the Galerkin expansion with respect to the L2 norm and vertical truncation at level 2, and with the leading order barotropic mode included, is a reasonable model of the data.

the system with the lowest vertical truncation (the barotropic mode only) and with the Galerkin truncation at the second order, is the most appropriate for studying the baroclinic dynamics of the Martian atmosphere.

the POD-Galerkin model with a vertical truncation at the leading order barotropic and baroclinic mode, with the L2-norm, and with a Galerkin truncation at the barotropic mode, most closely resembles the original diagnostics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the POD-Galerkin system is a good approximation of the full system, and that the system with a 3-mode vertical truncation and the Galerkin truncation of the barotropic and leading baroclinic mode is the best of the systems we have considered.
the 3-mode truncation of the 5-mode Galerkin expansion, using a weighted Euclidean norm, is the most appropriate for our data.

we are able to reproduce the original data with a high degree of accuracy, but that the most accurate results are obtained when the vertical structure of the model is truncated at the leading baroclinic mode, and when a Galerkin truncation is used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inclusion of topography and the use of the L2-norm are crucial for the model to be a good fit to the data.
, for the model considered, the barotropic mode is the only one that is necessary for the reproduction of the data, and that a Galerkin truncation of 2 is sufficient.

a Galerkin expansion in which both vertical and horizontal truncations are considered can provide a more accurate representation of the data than a Galerkin system that only considers vertical truncations.
